why: Tests a categorical positive/negative/neutral organization without assuming ordered distances among the three valence classes.
Tests an ordered hedonic axis rather than three unrelated valence classes.
Tests whether the dominant representational division is emotional salience rather than emotion identity or valence.
Targets a threat/negative-affect representation without requiring positive and neutral categories to differ.
Tests an action-tendency account that differs from valence because anger is predicted to align with approach rather than fear.
Tests whether neural geometry follows a plausible arousal ordering independently of valence.
Directly tests species-general emotion coding; the cross scope is the cleanest version.
Checks that species-general emotion correspondence is not driven by the perceptual distinctiveness of neutral stimuli.
Tests whether the two positive categories have distinct, species-general representations rather than a single positive cluster.
Tests whether threat-related categories retain distinct, species-general representations.
Tests whether valence organization survives without the potentially distinctive neutral condition.
Tests whether stimulus species is the dominant organizing dimension.
Tests a mixed representational geometry rather than forcing either species or emotion to dominate.
Provides a directional alternative in which emotion correspondence dominates species identity.
Provides a directional alternative in which species identity dominates emotion correspondence.
Tests a mixed geometry in which both species and three-category valence organize responses.
Provides a directional alternative in which valence dominates species identity.
Provides a directional alternative in which species identity dominates valence.
Emotion identity (5-way): same emotion=0, different=1.
Valence 3-class: same {pos|neg|neu}=0, different=1.
Valence binary: positive vs negative=1, within=0; Neutral excluded.
Emotional vs Neutral: any emotion grouped together vs Neutral.
Threat: {Anger,Fear} vs {others}.
Approach {P,H} vs Avoid {A,F}=1, within=0; Neutral excluded.
Graded valence: pos->neu->neg axis, adjacent=0.5, opposite=1.
Graded arousal: {A,F}=high, {P,H}=mid, {N}=low; adjacent=0.5, far=1.
Agent species shown: Dog-shown vs Hum-shown (emotion ignored).
